properties.headline: Flash Flood Warning issued October 15 at 3:59PM CDT until October 15 at 7:00PM CDT by NWS San Angelo TX
properties.description:
FFWSJT

The National Weather Service in San Angelo has issued a

* Flash Flood Warning for...
Southeastern Nolan County in west central Texas...
Southwestern Taylor County in west central Texas...

* Until 700 PM CDT.

* At 359 PM CDT, Doppler radar indicated thunderstorms producing
heavy rain across the warned area. Between 2 and 3 inches of rain
have fallen. Additional rainfall amounts up to 1 inch are possible
in the warned area. Flash flooding is ongoing or expected to begin
shortly.

HAZARD...Flash flooding caused by thunderstorms.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Flash flooding of small creeks and streams, urban areas,
highways, streets and underpasses as well as other poor
drainage and low-lying areas.

* Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...
Nolan, Happy Valley, Coronados Camp, Hylton, Camp Butman and Shep.

This includes the following Low Water Crossings...
FM 89 crossing Elm Creek, crossings along County Road 263, crossings
along County Road 357, County Road 196 crossing North Fork Valley
Creek, County Road 387 crossing Little Bitter Creek, crossings along
County Road 335, County Road 196 crossing North Fork Valley Creek,
crossings along County Road 283, crossings along County Road 301 and
County Road 263 crossing Fish Creek.
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

properties.headline: Red Flag Warning issued October 15 at 1:50PM PDT until October 16 at 11:00AM PDT by NWS Eureka CA
properties.description:
The National Weather Service in Eureka has issued a Red Flag
Warning, which is in effect from 10 PM this evening to 11 AM PDT
Friday. The Fire Weather Watch is no longer in effect.


* AFFECTED AREA...Fire weather zones 418 including Lake Pillsbury,
419 including the City of Clearlake, Middletown, Lower Lake,
Indian Valley Reservoir, and other areas in eastern and southern
Lake County. This will be mainly over the higher terrain.

* WIND...Sustained winds of 15-20mph with gusts to 30 mph possible
in exposed areas.

* HUMIDITY...Low overnight recoveries of 30-35% will drop to
10- 20% through the morning. Very poor RH recovery into
Friday.

* IMPACTS...any fires that develop will likely spread rapidly.
properties.instruction:
A Red Flag Warning means that critical fire weather conditions
are either occurring now, or will shortly. A combination of
strong winds, low relative humidity, and warm temperatures can
contribute to extreme fire behavior.

properties.headline: Special Weather Statement issued October 15 at 3:42PM CDT by NWS San Angelo TX
properties.description:
At 340 PM CDT, Doppler radar was tracking strong thunderstorms along
a line extending from near Lake Fort Phantom Hill to Tuscola.
Movement was east at 25 mph.

HAZARD...Wind gusts up to 50 mph.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Gusty winds could knock down tree limbs and blow around
unsecured objects.

Locations impacted include...
Abilene, Clyde, Baird, Tuscola, Buffalo Gap, Lawn, Eula, Dudley,
Potosi, Hamby, Nugent, Oplin, Impact, Lake Abilene, Camp Tonkawa,
Lake Fort Phantom Hill, Us-283 Near The Callahan-
Shackelford County Line, Ovalo, and Kirby Lake.

This includes Interstate 20 between Mile Markers 282 and 310.
properties.instruction:
If outdoors, consider seeking shelter inside a building.

Torrential rainfall is also occurring with these storms and may lead
to localized flooding. Do not drive your vehicle through flooded
roadways.

properties.description:

expected.

* WHERE...San Gorgonio Pass near Banning.

* WHEN...Until midnight PDT Saturday Night.

* IMPACTS...Damaging winds will blow down trees and power lines.
Power outages are possible. Travel will be difficult, especially
for high profile vehicles.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Strongest winds will be on Friday. Winds
become more easterly Saturday.
properties.instruction:

or damaged by the wind.

NWSheadline: HIGH WIND WARNING REMAINS IN EFFECT UNTIL MIDNIGHT PDT SATURDAY NIGHT

properties.headline: Heat Advisory issued October 15 at 1:39PM PDT until October 17 at 8:00PM PDT by NWS San Diego CA
properties.description:
* WHAT...For the Wind Advisory, northeast winds 20 to 30 mph with
gusts 35 to 55 mph expected. Strongest winds will be near the
foothills and in canyons of the Santa Ana mountains, with gusts up
to 70 mph possible. For the Heat Advisory, temperatures up to 95
degrees

* WHERE...Orange County Inland Areas.

* WHEN...For the Heat Advisory, until 8 PM PDT Saturday. For the Wind
Advisory, until noon PDT Saturday.

* IMPACTS...Gusty winds will blow around unsecured objects. Tree
limbs could be blown down and a few power outages may result.
Moderate to locally major HeatRisk. Those sensitive to heat may be
impacted.
properties.instruction:
Winds this strong can make driving difficult, especially for high
profile vehicles. Use extra caution.

Drink plenty of fluids, stay in an air-conditioned room, stay out of
the sun, and check up on relatives and neighbors.

Take extra precautions when outside. Wear lightweight and loose
fitting clothing. Try to limit strenuous activities to early morning
or evening. Take action when you see symptoms of heat exhaustion and
heat stroke.
